title: Hematology & Medical Oncology Fellowship
Department: Cleveland Clinic Cancer Institute (Taussig Cancer Center)
Deadline: Applications reviewed in July; submit by 31 July for interview consideration
Eligibility: Board eligible/board certified in internal medicine.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Main Match only (no positions outside the Match); interviews September-November
Funding: Cleveland Clinic GME benefits listed on programme page (e.g., $1,000 annual educational allowance; GME-funded meeting trip up to $2,500).
Summary: Since 1934, an intensive three-year ACGME-accredited combined haematology and medical oncology programme that has trained more than 200 graduates.

title: Hospice and Palliative Medicine Fellowship
Department: Cleveland Clinic Cancer Institute (Hospice and Palliative Medicine Program)
Deadline: Applications accepted during July each year (see NRMP for current-cycle deadlines)
Funding: Cleveland Clinic GME benefits listed on programme page (e.g., $1,000 annual educational allowance; GME-funded meeting trip up to $2,500).
Summary: Established in 1989 as the first US-based physician hospice and palliative medicine fellowship, training clinically excellent physicians, educators and scientists.

title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship
Department: Section of Geriatric Medicine
Deadline: Interviews July through November or until positions filled
Eligibility: Board-eligible or board-certified in Internal Medicine or Family Medicine.
Summary: A one-year clinical fellowship training physicians for leadership in geriatric medicine through outpatient GEM, inpatient consultation, teaching and research/QI.

title: Gastroenterology & Hepatology Fellowship
Department: Gastroenterology & Hepatology Fellowship Program (Cleveland Clinic digestive disease department)
Funding: NIH-funded T32 track; salaries based on level of training
Visa support: Cleveland Clinic accepts H-1B or ECFMG-sponsored J-1 visas for clinical fellowship; does not sponsor permanent residency petitions
Summary: A three-year ACGME-accredited programme with a categorical clinical/endoscopy track and an NIH T32 translational research track.

title: Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism Fellowship
Department: Endocrinology & Metabolism Institute / Medical Specialty Institute
Application method: ERAS only; NRMP Medical Specialties Matching Program; three letters
Funding: Year 1 appointed at PGY-4, year 2 at PGY-5
Summary: An ACGME-accredited endocrinology, diabetes and metabolism fellowship within Cleveland Clinic's Medical Specialty Institute.

title: Allergy and Clinical Immunology Fellowship
Department: Respiratory Institute
Eligibility: Board certified/eligible in Internal Medicine or Pediatrics.
Summary: A two-year allergy and clinical immunology fellowship with adult and paediatric continuity clinics, preparing graduates to practise independently.

title: Infectious Disease Fellowship
Department: Department of Infectious Disease
Eligibility: Completion of a US Internal Medicine residency.
Summary: A clinically oriented two-year ID fellowship with general, transplant/immunocompromised, endocarditis and bone and joint consult training at one of the largest US transplant centres.

title: Pulmonary & Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
Department: Respiratory Institute
Summary: After completing core board-eligibility requirements, PCCM fellows design a track suited to their goals, including additional clinical training, research or administrative experience.

title: Nephrology and Hypertension Fellowship
Department: Department of Kidney Medicine, Glickman Urological & Kidney Institute
Eligibility: Completed three-year ACGME-accredited Internal Medicine residency.
Application method: ERAS; programmes begin receiving applications 16 July 2026
Funding: NIH-funded U2C grant supports one research position per year
Visa support: Welcomes trainees on J-1 and H-1 visas
Summary: A two-year ACGME-accredited nephrology fellowship with categorical and research tracks plus optional AST and one-year ACGME transplant nephrology training.

title: Sleep Medicine Fellowship
Department: Sleep Disorders Center, Neurological Institute
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited programme at the Main Campus Sleep Disorders Center (over 25,000 sleep studies a year) with a 100% board pass rate since at least 2007.

title: Rheumatology Fellowship
Department: Orthopaedic & Rheumatologic Institute / Medical Specialties Institute
Eligibility: Foreign medical graduates must have completed a two-year US-based Internal Medicine residency before joining.
Application method: ERAS only; NRMP Medical Specialties Matching Program
Funding: Year 1 appointed at PGY-4, year 2 at PGY-5
Summary: A two-year ACGME-accredited rheumatology programme of 13 four-week modules per year with continuity clinic where fellows act as the patient's primary rheumatologist.

title: Endocrinology Fellowship
Department: Division of Endocrinology, Metabolism & Nutrition, Department of Medicine
Deadline: Applications reviewed in late July; interviews late August-October
Application method: ERAS (Clinical and Research Tracks); NRMP Match; programme signals considered; virtual interviews
Visa support: Rarely sponsors H-1B or J-1 visas (not supported by T32 grant), though well-qualified candidates needing sponsorship are encouraged to apply.
Summary: Duke's endocrinology fellowship offers separate Clinical and Research Tracks preparing fellows for clinical practice, research careers or academic clinician-educator roles.

title: Gastroenterology Fellowship
Department: Division of Gastroenterology, Department of Medicine
Deadline: Applications from July; interviews September-early October
Eligibility: IMGs must have completed an ACGME-accredited Internal Medicine residency and be ABIM board-eligible in Internal Medicine.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match; three letters incl. one from residency Chair/Programme Director; USMLE Steps 1-3
Funding: Research track supported by T32 grant
Visa support: J-1 supported on clinical track; H-1B not supported; visa holders not eligible for the T32-funded Research Track.
Summary: A three-year general gastroenterology and hepatology programme with clinical and T32-supported research tracks across tertiary, VA and community hospitals.

title: Geriatrics Fellowship
Department: Division of Geriatrics, Department of Medicine
International applicants: ECFMG status report required if applicable.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match; USMLE Steps 1-3 or COMLEX
Summary: Trains physicians to become expert clinicians and leaders in clinical work, research and education in geriatrics within a programme with over 40 years of experience.

title: Hematology-Oncology Fellowship
Department: Divisions of Medical Oncology, Hematological Malignancies and Cellular Therapy, and Hematology
Eligibility: Must have passed USMLE Step 3 (or equivalent) to enter at PGY-3 level or higher (Duke University Hospital policy).
International applicants: NIH-funded years 2-3 restricted to US citizens/permanent residents; other candidates considered if fully funded by their government or medical school.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match; four letters requested (one from residency programme director)
Positions: Average of 21 fellows across all training years
Funding: Years 2-3 primarily NIH-funded; Programme page refers to Duke Graduate Medical Education for stipends and benefits.
Summary: Provides clinical, translational and basic laboratory training in haematology, medical oncology, cell therapy and bone marrow transplantation with over 100 faculty and the Duke Cancer Institute.

title: Hospice & Palliative Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Medicine (Hospice and Palliative Medicine)
Application method: ERAS only; NRMP Match; virtual interviews
Summary: Established in 2005, a one-year ACGME-accredited programme training future leaders in hospice and palliative medicine across inpatient and outpatient settings with mentoring from national leaders.

title: Infectious Diseases Fellowship
Department: Division of Infectious Diseases, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: IMGs require completion of ACGME-accredited (or equivalent) IM residency and ABIM board-eligibility in IM.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Specialties Matching Program; virtual interviews
Funding: Programme page refers to Duke Graduate Medical Education for stipends and benefits.
Visa support: Accepts applicants sponsored on ECFMG J-1 clinical visas
Summary: A three-year programme with a clinical first year at Duke University Medical Center and Durham VA followed by research training, with over 80% of graduates in academic ID faculty positions.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
Department: Division of Nephrology, Department of Medicine
Deadline: ERAS from July 2026; interviews late August-October; Match Day 2 December 2026
Eligibility: All three USMLE Steps (or COMLEX equivalent) passed before start.
Application method: ERAS only; NRMP 'all in' Match; virtual Zoom interviews
Visa support: J-1 and H-1B sponsored for selected applicants
Summary: A fellow-driven nephrology programme with night float, integrated VA experience, clinical concentrations and clinical/biomedical investigator pathways.

title: Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
Department: Division of Pulmonary, Allergy and Critical Care Medicine, Department of Medicine
Summary: A three-year combined PCCM fellowship producing physicians prepared for academic careers, with dual-certification eligibility and an optional fourth research year.

title: Rheumatology Fellowship
Department: Division of Rheumatology and Immunology, Department of Medicine
Application method: ERAS only; NRMP Match; programme signalling; virtual interviews
Summary: Trains rheumatologists for private practice, clinician-educator and physician-scientist careers within a top-ranked Division of Rheumatology and Immunology.

title: Gastroenterology Fellowship Training Program
Department: Division of Digestive Diseases, Department of Medicine
Summary: A three-year ACGME-accredited programme producing board-certified digestive disease subspecialists and clinical investigators, with further training available in advanced endoscopy and transplant hepatology.

title: Endocrinology Fellowship
Department: Division of Endocrinology, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed residency in Internal Medicine and eligible for ABIM internal medicine board exam.
Application method: ERAS only; NRMP Match; required interviews August-November
Funding: Each fellow receives funds to travel to a national endocrine meeting yearly
Summary: A two-year endocrinology fellowship with rotations at Emory University Hospital, Emory Midtown, Grady and the Atlanta VA, with strengths in pituitary, bone, lipid, thyroid and diabetes care.

title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship
Department: Division of Geriatrics and Gerontology, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Residents trained in internal or family medicine in the United States.
International applicants: Foreign medical graduates accepted with valid ECFMG certification and US ACGME-accredited IM or FM residency.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match (applicants accepted only through the Match except in extraordinary circumstances)
Summary: A 12-month ACGME-accredited clinical programme training fellows in direct and consultative care of diverse older patients at the Atlanta VA, Emory Healthcare and Grady.

title: Infectious Diseases Fellowship
Department: Division of Infectious Diseases, Department of Medicine
Summary: Develops exceptional clinicians and scholars in infectious diseases, with a clinical first year and a second year focused on mentored scholarship in areas such as HIV, transplant ID and stewardship.

title: Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
Department: Division of Pulmonary, Allergy, Critical Care, and Sleep Medicine, Department of Medicine
Summary: Emory's PCCM fellowship recruits six fellows annually for three to four years of clinical and research training.

title: Sleep Medicine Fellowship
Department: Division of Pulmonary, Allergy, Critical Care, and Sleep Medicine, Department of Medicine
Summary: A comprehensive one-year fellowship combining hands-on clinical sleep medicine experience across multiple sites with a foundation in scholarly pursuits.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
Department: Division of Renal Medicine, Department of Medicine
Summary: Trains outstanding clinical nephrologists and renal physician-scientists across Emory University Hospital, Emory Midtown, Atlanta VA, Grady Memorial and Emory St. Joseph's.

title: Rheumatology Fellowship
Department: Division of Rheumatology, Department of Medicine
Summary: A two-year ACGME-accredited programme rotating across four tertiary hospitals with specialised clinics, a musculoskeletal ultrasound curriculum and paediatric rheumatology exposure.

title: Hospice and Palliative Medicine Fellowship
Department: Division of General Medicine and Geriatrics, Department of Medicine
Summary: An ACGME-accredited one-year fellowship founded in 2010 that trains leaders in palliative medicine clinical care, research and education across multiple sites with more than 25 faculty.

title: Hematology and Medical Oncology Fellowship
Department: Department of Hematology and Medical Oncology
Summary: An ACGME-accredited three-year combined programme (plus a hematology-focused track) training haematologists and oncologists to lead clinical and translational research, with mentored research time.

title: Rheumatology Fellowship (Minnesota)
inst: Mayo Clinic School of Graduate Medical Education
Department: Mayo Clinic School of Graduate Medical Education (Rochester campus)
Summary: A two-year rheumatology fellowship at Mayo Clinic in Rochester with an optional research-focused third year and CCaTS certificate or master's coursework.

title: Infectious Diseases Fellowship (Minnesota)
inst: Mayo Clinic School of Graduate Medical Education
Department: Mayo Clinic School of Graduate Medical Education (Rochester campus)
Funding: Institutional funding guaranteed for the dedicated research year
Summary: A three-year ID fellowship offering in-depth training in clinical practice, education and research, with guaranteed funding for a dedicated research year and a 2:1 faculty-to-fellow ratio.

title: Hematology and Medical Oncology Fellowship (Minnesota)
inst: Mayo Clinic School of Graduate Medical Education
Department: Mayo Clinic School of Graduate Medical Education (Rochester campus)
Positions: About 10 trainees complete the programme annually
Summary: A three-year combined haematology and medical oncology fellowship at Mayo Clinic's Rochester campus leading to ABIM eligibility in both subspecialties.

title: Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine Fellowship (Minnesota)
inst: Mayo Clinic School of Graduate Medical Education
Department: Mayo Clinic School of Graduate Medical Education (Rochester campus)
Summary: A three-year PCCM fellowship emphasising clinical training and research, customised to each fellow, in which fellows perform their own ICU intubations and airway management.

title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship (Minnesota)
inst: Mayo Clinic School of Graduate Medical Education
Department: Mayo Clinic School of Graduate Medical Education (Rochester campus)
Duration: 12 months (Path A) or 12 months plus a non-ACGME academic year (Path B)
Summary: An ACGME-accredited geriatric medicine fellowship with a 12-month clinical pathway and an optional additional academic year.

title: Infectious Diseases Fellowship (Combined MGH-BWH)
inst: Mass General Brigham (combined Massachusetts General Hospital and Brigham and Women's Hospital programme)
Department: Division of Infectious Diseases, Mass General Brigham
Duration: 2 years (board eligibility); optional further T32-supported research years
Deadline: Apply through ERAS July-August; interviews 22 & 28 September, 5 & 13 October 2026; Match Day 2 December 2026
Summary: A combined MGH-BWH programme training leaders in infectious diseases, with a first clinical year across both hospitals, Mass Eye and Ear and Dana-Farber, and clinician-educator or research pathways.

title: Gastroenterology Fellowship at Massachusetts General Hospital
Department: Mass General Brigham Division of Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Endoscopy
Deadline: Third Wednesday in July (ERAS); interviews September-October
Eligibility: Enrolled in or completed an ACGME-accredited internal medicine residency; minimum 18 months clinical curriculum.
International applicants: Graduates of international medical schools (except Canadian) need 6-12 months of US-based hands-on clinical experience and three letters from US medical school faculty.
Visa support: J-1 and H-1B visa applicants considered on occasion
Licence requirement: Licence issued by the Medical Board of Massachusetts required
Summary: Provides a rigorous foundation in patient care, research and teaching for physicians committed to academic gastroenterology, with access to opportunities across the integrated Mass General Brigham division.

title: MGH Rheumatology Fellowship
Department: Mass General Brigham Division of Rheumatology, Inflammation and Immunity
Duration: 2 years (ACGME clinical pathway) or 3 years (NIH-sponsored track)
Eligibility: Three years of IM postgraduate training (or two under the research residency pathway); board eligible in IM; USMLE Steps I-III passed.
Summary: Trains academic rheumatologists as clinicians, clinician-educators and clinician-scientists, with inpatient consults at MGH and Mass Eye and Ear and over 12,000 outpatient visits a year.

title: Allergy & Immunology Fellowship
inst: Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine (McGaw Medical Center)
Department: Division of Allergy & Immunology, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-approved residency in Medicine, Pediatrics or Med-Peds.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match; programme signalling encouraged but not required
Positions: 4 MD or DO fellows per year
Summary: A two-year ACGME-accredited fellowship (50% clinical, 25% research, 25% education) training leaders in academic allergy and immunology, with a 100% ABAI pass rate since 2002.

title: Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism Fellowship
inst: Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine (McGaw Medical Center)
Department: Department of Medicine (Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism)
Eligibility: At least two years of ACGME-accredited IM postgraduate training; board-eligible in IM at start; USMLE Steps 1-3 passed.
Funding: NIH T32 supports most fellows during research years
Visa support: J-1 holders considered only for two-year clinical track; H-1B not considered; T32 positions and third year limited to US citizens/permanent residents
Licence requirement: Eligible for Illinois medical license; temporary license required
Summary: Prepares physicians for academic and clinical endocrinology careers through two years of clinical training and clinical, translational or basic research.

title: Gastroenterology & Hepatology Fellowship
inst: Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine (McGaw Medical Center)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology & Hepatology, Department of Medicine
Duration: 3 years (clinical, T32 research, or dual GI/transplant hepatology track)
Eligibility: Minimum two years ACGME-accredited IM postgraduate training; board eligibility in IM at entry.
International applicants: IMGs require a valid ECFMG certificate and J-1, H-1B or permanent resident status.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match; four letters incl. one from residency programme
Positions: 3-5 fellows per year (1-2 general GI, 1-2 T32 research, 1 transplant hepatology)
Licence requirement: Eligible for unrestricted Illinois medical license
Summary: A three-year fellowship providing a comprehensive foundation in clinical care and investigative research, with more than 75% of graduates entering academic positions.

title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship
inst: Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine (McGaw Medical Center)
Department: Department of Medicine (Geriatrics)
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-accredited IM or FM residency; ABIM exam eligible; USMLE I, II and III passed at time of application.
International applicants: Valid ECFMG certification required if applicable.
Visa support: Applicants must be US citizen, permanent resident or hold a J-1 visa
Licence requirement: Eligible for unrestricted Illinois medical license
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship with rotations at Northwestern Memorial Hospital and Shirley Ryan AbilityLab, providing excellence in clinical geriatrics, teaching and research.

title: Hematology & Medical Oncology Fellowship
inst: Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine (McGaw Medical Center)
Department: Division of Hematology and Oncology, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Only residents in an ACGME-accredited residency in a US hospital are considered.
International applicants: Non-permanent residents must already hold a visa permitting a three-year stay (usually J).
Application method: ERAS only; NRMP Match; virtual interviews September 2026
Licence requirement: Valid Illinois permanent license required for appointment
Summary: Trains and mentors academic leaders in medical oncology and haematology over three years at McGaw Medical Center, leading to dual board eligibility.

title: Infectious Diseases Fellowship
inst: Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine (McGaw Medical Center)
Department: Division of Infectious Diseases, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed approved US residency providing ABIM eligibility in Internal Medicine.
Application method: ERAS from July; three letters; interviews August-October; NRMP Match
Visa support: J-1 holders considered only for two-year clinical track; H-1B not considered; T32 and third-year positions limited to US citizens/permanent residents
Summary: A two-year programme with a clinical first year and a highly customisable second year, plus optional mentored research supported by T32 and foundation funding.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine (McGaw Medical Center)
Department: Division of Nephrology & Hypertension, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-accredited residency; ABIM exam eligible before start.
International applicants: Valid ECFMG certification and valid visa required if applicable.
Application method: ERAS only; NRMP Match; interviews from end of August
Licence requirement: Eligible for unrestricted medical license before training
Summary: A two-year nephrology fellowship with nine months on the Northwestern Memorial inpatient consult service in year one, VA training, scholarly tracks and an integrated nephrology-critical care option.

title: Pulmonary & Critical Care Clinical Fellowship
inst: Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine (McGaw Medical Center)
Department: Division of Pulmonary & Critical Care Medicine, Department of Medicine
Deadline: Previous cycle deadline 16 July (July 2026 start); current-cycle date not stated
Eligibility: Enrolled in or completed ACGME-accredited internal medicine residency.
Application method: ERAS only; NRMP Medical Specialties Matching Program
Visa support: ECFMG-sponsored J-1 (McGaw sponsoring institution); J-1 fees paid by applicant
Summary: A three-year combined PCCM fellowship meeting ABIM requirements in both specialties, with continuity clinics at Northwestern and Jesse Brown VA and research opportunities.

title: Rheumatology Fellowship
inst: Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine (McGaw Medical Center)
Department: Division of Rheumatology, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-accredited Internal Medicine residency; ABIM exam eligible; US citizen/national or permanent resident (T32 support).
International applicants: US citizenship, non-citizen national or permanent residence required (NIH T32).
Licence requirement: Eligible for unrestricted Illinois medical license
Summary: A two-year curriculum preparing fellows for ABIM rheumatology certification, with research or medical education emphasis in year two and an optional T32-supported research year.

title: Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism Fellowship
inst: NYU Grossman School of Medicine / NYU Langone Health
Department: Holman Division of Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Three years of accredited postgraduate education in internal medicine before fellowship.
International applicants: Valid ECFMG certificate required for graduates of medical schools outside the US.
Application method: ERAS only; three letters incl. residency programme director; programme signalling
Summary: A two-year ACGME-accredited fellowship offering experience in patient care, research and teaching across all aspects of endocrinology, diabetes and metabolism.

title: Gastroenterology & Hepatology Three-Year Clinical Fellowship
inst: NYU Grossman School of Medicine / NYU Langone Health
Department: Division of Gastroenterology & Hepatology, Department of Medicine
Summary: A three-year ACGME-accredited clinical fellowship leading to mastery of gastroenterology and endoscopic procedures, with rotations across four hospital sites and outpatient locations.

title: Hematology & Medical Oncology Fellowship
inst: NYU Grossman School of Medicine / NYU Langone Health
Department: Division of Hematology & Medical Oncology, Department of Medicine / Perlmutter Cancer Center
Deadline: Application cycle runs from July 2026 through mid-August 2026
International applicants: ECFMG status report required if applicable.
Application method: ERAS only with programme signalling; virtual interviews September-October 2026; no prematch
Summary: A three-year combined fellowship training academic physicians in haematology and medical oncology with clinical and research expertise, in collaboration with Perlmutter Cancer Center.

title: Infectious Diseases & Immunology Fellowship
inst: NYU Grossman School of Medicine / NYU Langone Health
Department: Division of Infectious Diseases & Immunology, Department of Medicine
Application method: ERAS only; three letters incl. programme director or chair
Visa support: NYU Langone does not offer H-1B sponsorship for house staff, residents or fellows; J-1 sponsorship available through ECFMG.
Summary: A two-year ACGME-accredited ID fellowship with diverse clinical experiences and optional formal research training, plus transplant ID and other concentrations.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: NYU Grossman School of Medicine / NYU Langone Health
Department: Division of Nephrology, Department of Medicine
Deadline: Rolling review; interview contacts after 15 July
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Medical Specialties Matching Program
Summary: A two-year ACGME-accredited nephrology fellowship following a 21st-century curriculum that prepares fellows for the ABIM nephrology examination.

title: Pulmonary & Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
inst: NYU Grossman School of Medicine / NYU Langone Health
Department: Division of Pulmonary, Critical Care & Sleep Medicine, Department of Medicine
Application method: ERAS; three letters incl. programme director or chair
Visa support: NYU Langone does not offer H-1B sponsorship for house staff, residents or fellows; J-1 sponsorship available through ECFMG.
Summary: A three-year ACGME-accredited programme meeting pulmonary and critical care board requirements and individualised to each fellow's career path.

title: Sleep Medicine Fellowship
inst: NYU Grossman School of Medicine / NYU Langone Health
Department: Division of Pulmonary, Critical Care & Sleep Medicine, Department of Medicine
Visa support: NYU Langone does not offer H-1B sponsorship for house staff, residents or fellows; J-1 sponsorship available through ECFMG.
Summary: Prepares fellows for academic or clinical sleep medicine careers with training at Bellevue, VA NY Harbor, NYU Langone ambulatory clinics and Tisch Hospital.

title: Rheumatology Fellowship
inst: NYU Grossman School of Medicine / NYU Langone Health
Department: Division of Rheumatology, Department of Medicine
Funding: Research track supported by T32 training grant and/or other sources
Summary: A two-year ACGME-accredited rheumatology fellowship within one of the premier US rheumatology divisions, with an optional research track.

title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship (Stanford-VA Palo Alto)
Department: Section of Geriatric Medicine, Department of Medicine; VA Palo Alto Health Care System GRECC
Deadline: Applications open in July via ERAS; interviews August-October; NRMP rank list deadline in November (no fixed closing date stated)
Eligibility: Completion of an ACGME or AOA accredited residency in Family Medicine or Internal Medicine by fellowship start; certified or actively pursuing board certification in primary specialty; USMLE/COMLEX Steps 1-3.
International applicants: IMGs accepted with ECFMG certification; applicants must be US citizens, permanent residents or hold a J-1 visa.
Visa support: J-1 only; Stanford does not sponsor H-1B visas for international medical graduates.
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited joint Stanford University and VA Palo Alto Health Care System fellowship, administered by the Palo Alto VA GRECC, that prepares fellows to become skilled practitioners and leaders in Geriatric Medicine.

title: Rheumatology Fellowship
Department: Division of Immunology & Rheumatology, Department of Medicine
Deadline: Applications accepted via ERAS from July 2026 for 2027 positions; interviews start September 2026
Eligibility: Three years of postgraduate training in Internal Medicine (or two years under the ABIM Research Pathway); Board Eligible in Internal Medicine at start; USMLE I, II and III passed (waivers considered individually).

Funding: Stanford GME offers salaries matched to the Bay Area cost of living; programme page refers to the Stanford GME website for salaries and benefits.
Summary: Stanford's rheumatology fellowship trains rheumatologists for careers in immunology, clinical rheumatology or clinical epidemiology of rheumatic diseases, combining cutting-edge science with compassionate care.

title: Hospice & Palliative Medicine Fellowship
Department: Hospice & Palliative Medicine Fellowship Program, Stanford Medicine
Eligibility: Completed residency in child neurology, family medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics, Med/Peds, PM&R, neurology or radiation oncology; or at least three clinical years of anesthesiology, emergency medicine, OB/GYN, psychiatry, radiology or surgery residency.

Visa support: Stanford can sponsor J-1 visas through its International Students and Scholars Office.
Licence requirement: California medical license required before starting
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship with clinical sites spanning an inpatient hospice unit, a safety-net hospital, an academic medical center, long-term care and home-based hospice care.

title: Sleep Medicine Fellowship
Department: Division of Sleep Medicine, Stanford Medicine
Eligibility: Board eligible or certified in Internal Medicine, Neurology, Psychiatry, Pediatrics, Otolaryngology, Family Medicine or Anesthesia through an ACGME-accredited programme.
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited clinical sleep medicine fellowship sponsored by Stanford Hospital and Clinics at the Stanford Sleep Medicine Center, the first fellowship programme accredited by the American Sleep Disorders Association.

title: Clinical Informatics Fellowship
Department: Clinical Informatics Fellowship Program, Stanford Medicine
Deadline: ERAS applications accepted early July to 14 September 2026; AMIA match 17 December 2026
Eligibility: For AY2027-28, candidates trained in emergency medicine, internal medicine or pediatrics.
International applicants: Foreign medical graduates may apply; certified English translation of transcript required.

Application method: ERAS (listed under Clinical Informatics (Pediatrics)); AMIA Clinical Informatics Match
Summary: Stanford's ACGME-accredited clinical informatics fellowship offers applied clinical informatics experiences across Stanford Medicine, local health systems and industry.

title: Blood & Marrow Transplantation and Cellular Therapy Fellowship
Department: Division of Blood & Marrow Transplantation & Cellular Therapy, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed fellowship in Hematology or Oncology (rarely, completion of Internal Medicine residency considered).
Application method: Direct application: CV and three letters of support to the Program Director; in-person or Zoom interview
Licence requirement: Must be able to obtain a California medical license
Summary: A one-year clinical fellowship in hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapy that has trained more than 45 physicians since 2007.

title: Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism Fellowship (UCLA-VA)
inst: UCLA Health / David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA
Department: Division of Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism, Department of Medicine
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match (NRMP code 1956143F0); programme signalling considered
Summary: The UCLA-VA Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism Fellowship is a two-year programme offering clinical and research training at Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center, Santa Monica UCLA Medical Center and the VA Greater Los Angeles Health Care System.

title: Digestive Diseases (Gastroenterology) Fellowship
inst: UCLA Health / David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA

Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match; programme signalling preferred
Licence requirement: Valid California medical license, or eligible to apply for one by 1 July
Summary: One of the largest GI training programmes, offering clinical and research training across academic, VA, county and community hospitals with clinical and research scholar tracks.

title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship (UCLA-VA Multicampus)
inst: UCLA Health / David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA
Department: Division of Geriatric Medicine, Department of Medicine

Visa support: H-1B and J-1 visa sponsorship offered
Licence requirement: California medical license within 180 days of enrolment
Summary: A one-year UCLA-VA geriatric medicine fellowship with training across UCLA Health, the Greater Los Angeles VA and Harbor-UCLA, plus community nursing homes and a PACE centre, with optional inpatient, SNF and home-based pathways.

title: Hematology & Oncology Fellowship
inst: UCLA Health / David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA
Department: Division of Hematology-Oncology, Department of Medicine
Application method: ERAS (ERAS code 155-05-21-123); NRMP Match; at least four letters including one from programme director
Summary: A three-year ACGME-accredited combined haematology and oncology programme with 18 months of clinical service and 18 months of dedicated research, aimed at developing academic leaders.

title: Hospice and Palliative Medicine Fellowship
inst: UCLA Health / David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA
Department: UCLA Health Palliative Care
Application method: ERAS; three letters of recommendation (one from programme director); virtual interviews
Funding: All fellows reimbursed at the PGY-4 level regardless of training years
Licence requirement: Active California medical license required by 1 July
Summary: UCLA's hospice and palliative medicine fellowship trains clinically excellent physicians in managing physical, psychological and spiritual distress within interdisciplinary care, with the Greater Los Angeles VA as a participating site.

title: Infectious Diseases Fellowship (UCLA Multicampus Program)
inst: UCLA Health / David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA

Department: Section of Nephrology, Department of Internal Medicine
Eligibility: Completed three-year ACGME-accredited internal medicine residency by fellowship start.
Application method: ERAS only; interview slots allocated by timing of receipt
Summary: A two-year nephrology academic clinician track focused on clinical skills, teaching and education, with inpatient rotations in year one and flexible inpatient/outpatient training in year two.

title: Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
Department: Section of Pulmonary, Critical Care and Sleep Medicine, Department of Internal Medicine
Duration: 3 years (36 months; option to extend for research)
Eligibility: Completed accredited three-year internal medicine residency.
Funding: Division T32 NIH training grant supports advanced research training
Summary: A three-year PCCM fellowship with at least 18 months of clinical training and 18 months of scholarly activity, supported by an NIH T32 grant.

title: ACGME Adult Infectious Diseases Fellowship
inst: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine
Department: Division of Infectious Diseases, Department of Medicine
Duration: Typically 3 years (year 1 clinical; later years research)
Summary: Founded in 1981, a fellowship that typically spans three years with a clinical first year followed by research, preparing fellows for careers in academic medicine and public health.

title: Gastroenterology Fellowship
inst: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine
Department: Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology, Department of Medicine
Summary: A three-year fellowship with clinical and research tracks at The Johns Hopkins Hospital and Johns Hopkins Bayview, training leaders in academic and clinical gastroenterology.

title: Infectious Diseases Fellowship
inst: University of Michigan Medical School (Michigan Medicine)
Department: Division of Infectious Diseases, Department of Internal Medicine
Deadline: ERAS opens early July; programme receives applications mid-July; virtual interviews August-October
Application method: ERAS; three letters (one from programme director or chair)
Visa support: Minimum J-1 visa status required; H-1B applicants not considered
Summary: An ACGME-accredited programme blending clinical and research training at University Hospital and the VA Ann Arbor, with tracks in medical education, transplant ID, antimicrobial stewardship and research.

title: Infectious Diseases Fellowship
Department: Division of Infectious Diseases, Department of Medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (UCSF Department of Medicine lists 21 ACGME-accredited fellowships)
Funding: Research supported by multiple NIH T32 training grants
Summary: UCSF's ID fellowship trains leaders in research, public health, global health, stewardship, clinical ID and education across UCSF Medical Center, Zuckerberg San Francisco General and the SF VA.
